title.en: Prepare a BRS starting from an overdraft

say.en: Many traders use an overdraft: the bank lets them withdraw more than they have. The reconciliation still works if we treat the overdraft as a negative balance. In this lesson: Prepare a BRS starting from an overdraft.
Interpret a minus result.

body.en: An *overdraft* is a credit balance in the cash book and a debit balance in the pass book. Start the statement with the overdraft and treat it as a minus figure, apply exactly the same rules as for a favourable balance, and if the result is negative it is again an overdraft. Equivalently, every item that would be added to a favourable balance is deducted from the overdraft, and vice versa.
body.kn: ಓವರ್‌ಡ್ರಾಫ್ಟ್ ನಗದು ಪುಸ್ತಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್, ಪಾಸ್ ಪುಸ್ತಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಡೆಬಿಟ್ ಶಿಲ್ಕು. ಅದನ್ನು ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಮೊತ್ತವಾಗಿ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಅದೇ ನಿಯಮಗಳನ್ನು ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿ; ಉತ್ತರ ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕವಾದರೆ ಅದು ಓವರ್‌ಡ್ರಾಫ್ಟ್.

problem.en: Pass book of Gowda Traders shows an overdraft of ₹15,000 on 31 March. Cheques issued ₹3,000 were not presented; cheques deposited ₹5,000 were not cleared; interest on overdraft ₹600 was charged by the bank but not entered in the cash book. Find the overdraft as per cash book.

steps.en: Cheques issued not presented: the cash book is lower → −3,000 → −18,000.
Cheques deposited not cleared: the cash book is higher → +5,000 → −13,000.
Interest charged only in the pass book: the cash book is higher → +600 → −12,400.

Cheques issued ₹3,000 were not presented; cheques deposited ₹5,000 were not cleared; interest on overdraft ₹600 was charged by the bank but not entered in the cash book. Find the overdraft as per cash book.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Pass book of Gowda Traders shows an overdraft of 15,000 rupees on 31 March. Cheques issued 3,000 rupees were not presented; cheques deposited 5,000 rupees were not cleared; interest on overdraft 600 rupees was charged by the bank but not entered in the cash book. Find the overdraft as per cash book.
Start: pass book balance equals minus 15,000 overdraft.
Cheques issued not presented: the cash book is lower gives minus 3,000 gives minus 18,000.
Cheques deposited not cleared: the cash book is higher gives plus 5,000 gives minus 13,000.
Interest charged only in the pass book: the cash book is higher gives plus 600 gives minus 12,400.
So the answer is Overdraft as per cash book 12,400 rupees.

body.en: Treat a favourable balance as above zero and an overdraft as below zero. Every adjustment just moves the reading up or down; if you end below zero, the answer is an overdraft.
